brief: Weekly cross-asset monitor. After the Fed hike, UST 2Y yields rose 12bp; MS rates strategists argue the market-implied path overweights restrictive Fed policy persisting into late 2027, and recommend staying in SFRZ6Z7 flatteners. After the BoJ hike, USD/JPY rose 2.1%; MS FX strategists stay bearish the yen and see further upside in the pair, viewing relative policy stances as mispriced. The S&P 500 fell 0.1% on the week despite gains after the Fed hike; equity strategists expect quality leadership to continue but flag tactical downside risk from higher energy prices and the midterms. Brent fell 0.7% but touched $110/bbl intraday, with calendar spreads rallying as supply disruptions, falling inventories and stronger physical demand tighten the market. MS's Q2 2027 base case forecasts: S&P 500 8,300 (+9.6%) from 7,651; UST 10yr yield to 4.20% from 5.00%; Brent to $90; Gold to $4,900 from $4,473. The weekly monitor also shows Topix outperforming MSCI ACWI and the FTSEMIB, Healthcare leading over Materials, US IG tightening against EUR IG widening, France 10Y moving +2.5 SD, the UST curve twist-flattening, KRW moving -2.9 SD, DXY up 1.1%, and Silver outperforming broader commodities and iron ore.
